name: Process subcontract change orders
summary: Every owner change that touches subcontracted work, and every extra a trade claims on its own, has to become a priced and signed change to that trade's subcontract. The assistant project manager requests and reviews the trade's quote, the project manager negotiates and approves it, and the subcontract administrator issues it and updates the commitment in the ERP so the trade can bill. Changes recoverable from the owner wait for the owner change order, so trades often work for weeks before their change is signed, and revision cycles, unsigned time and materials tickets and disputed extras cause many lien and claim threats.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 220 active building projects and about 3,000 active subcontracts.
baseline.notes: Subcontracts are mostly CCA 1 style stipulated price subcontracts with change clauses mirroring the prime contract; changes are logged in a project management platform and committed in the construction ERP.

trigger: An owner change needs trade pricing, a subcontractor submits a change order request for an extra, or the site directs a trade to do extra work.
end_state: A signed subcontract change order is posted to the commitment in the ERP, or the request is rejected, cancelled with the owner change, or escalated as a trade dispute.

volume.seasonality: Follows owner changes: higher May to November.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate: about 1.3 trade changes per owner change event plus trade-initiated extras. Kept unchanged.

surge.cause: Public owner fiscal year-end change orders (February to March) flow down to trades

evidence.note: Author's estimate, following the owner change surge in gc-ops-change-order.
Logs, requests, reviews and drafts most trade changes; FTE is the author's estimate. Loaded cost from the organisation file (salaried wage x 1.35).
Negotiates, decides cost allocation and approves; FTE is the author's estimate. Loaded cost from the organisation file (salaried wage x 1.35).
Issues changes and keys commitments; FTE is the author's estimate (about a third of 22). Loaded cost from the organisation file (salaried wage x 1.35).
Verifies extras and signs time and materials tickets; FTE is the author's estimate. Loaded cost from the organisation file (salaried wage x 1.35).
Approves large changes and escalations; FTE is the author's estimate. Loaded cost from the organisation file (salaried wage x 1.35).

systems.name: Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Take-off and estimating software with Excel bid sheets
Field time capture (paper sheets or tablet app keyed to cost codes)
Subcontractor prequalification database (questionnaires, insurance and WSIB certificates)
Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)

steps.name: Log the subcontract change
steps.description: The assistant project manager opens a subcontract change record in the project platform, linked to the owner change event, a subcontractor's change order request or a site instruction. They record the trade, the subcontract number and the claimed or expected value.
inputs: owner change event, subcontractor change order request or site instruction

error.defect_description: Linked to the wrong owner change or subcontract.

evidence.note: Standard practice of linking trade changes to owner changes so cost and revenue match; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the subcontract scope
steps.description: The assistant project manager opens the subcontract, its scope of work, tender inclusions and exclusions and unit prices, and checks whether the work is already included. They decide whether to request pricing, verify a claimed extra on site, direct urgent work on time and materials or reject the request.

error.defect_description: Pays for work already in the subcontract scope.

next.condition: pricing needed for an owner change
urgent: proceed on time and materials

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimate; about a quarter of trade changes start as subcontractor claims for extras not covered by an owner change, as the organisation file describes.

steps.name: Verify the claimed extra on site
steps.description: The superintendent walks the area, compares the claimed work with daily reports, photos and any signed time and materials tickets, and confirms whether the work was outside the trade's scope and actually done. They record the finding in the change record.

evidence.note: Superintendents verify trade claims against site records; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request a quotation from the trade
steps.description: The assistant project manager sends the trade the change scope sheet and drawings and asks for a breakdown of labour hours, rates, materials, equipment and markup by a due date. The request refers to the subcontract change clause.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the subcontractor's priced request
steps.description: The subcontractor prices the change with its suppliers and sub-trades and returns a change order request. Specialty contractors report that preparing a fully priced request takes about three weeks on average after the field work is known.
inputs: request for quotation or signed time and materials tickets

evidence.note: Average 22 days from signed T&M tag to fully priced change order request (US survey, 2026); the range is the author's fit to that average.

steps.name: Chase the overdue quote
steps.description: The assistant project manager emails and phones the trade's project manager for the overdue quote and raises it in the weekly subcontractor meeting. The owner quotation cannot go out without it.

evidence.note: Missing subcontractor pricing delays contractor proposals for weeks or months.

steps.name: Review the quote breakdown
steps.description: The assistant project manager checks labour hours, rates, material prices and markups against the subcontract allowances and the company's own estimate, and checks for overlap with other trades. Quotes with errors or thin backup go back for revision.

error.defect_description: Excess markup or double counting missed.

evidence.note: More than half of change requests need two or more revision cycles; GCs cite disputed pricing (66%) and insufficient backup (53%). Branch shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate with the subcontractor
steps.description: The project manager meets or calls the trade's manager to settle hours, rates and scope gaps, sometimes trading against back-charges on the same subcontract. The agreed figure is noted in the change record.

error.defect_description: Concession not reflected in the owner quotation.

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Forward the trade price into the owner quotation
steps.description: The assistant project manager attaches the reviewed trade price to the owner change quotation and tells the trade that the subcontract change will be issued when the owner approves. The trade price is held open while the owner decides.

error.defect_description: Trade price not updated after negotiation.

evidence.note: The construction manager prices the contemplated change by obtaining subcontractor pricing for the owner.

steps.name: Wait for the owner change order
steps.description: The owner change works through consultant review, negotiation and signing, and the trade waits. When the owner approves, the subcontract change is issued; if the owner declines or cuts the change, the trade change is cancelled or renegotiated.

evidence.note: Owner review adds weeks (USACE median 55 days from proposal to modification); this owner mix is faster, so the mode is set at 14 days.

steps.name: Decide who bears the cost
steps.description: For changes the owner will not pay for, such as coordination errors or acceleration, the project manager decides whether to charge contingency, transfer budget between cost codes or back-charge another trade. They record the reason in the change record.

error.defect_description: Cost charged to the wrong code or a back-charge not raised.

control.basis: Company project controls policy: contingency drawdowns and budget transfers approved by the project manager and reported in the monthly forecast

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the subcontract change order
steps.description: The assistant project manager drafts the subcontract change order in the project platform with the scope description, agreed price, schedule effect, cost code and link to the owner change. They attach the trade quote as backup.
inputs: owner change order or cost allocation decision

error.defect_description: Wrong cost code or scope wording.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the subcontract change order
steps.description: The project manager checks the draft against the agreed price, the owner change and the budget, then approves it in the project platform. Values above the manager's limit go to the operations manager.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority for subcontract commitments

evidence.note: Threshold share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Operations manager approves a large change
steps.description: The operations manager reviews large subcontract changes for budget and contract risk and approves them by email or in the platform. Rejected drafts go back for rework.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority above the project manager limit

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue the change and update the commitment
steps.description: The subcontract administrator checks the approvals, confirms the trade's insurance and workers' compensation clearance are current, enters the commitment change in the ERP and generates the formal subcontract change order. They email it to the trade for signature.

error.defect_description: Commitment keyed with the wrong amount.

control.basis: Commitment changes keyed by subcontract administration only against a documented project manager approval

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate; WSIB clearance checks are standard for Ontario subcontract payments.

steps.name: Wait for the trade's signature
steps.description: The subcontractor reviews the change order, signs it and returns it by email. Trades sometimes hold the signature to argue over wording or reserve rights on time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the signed change order
steps.description: The subcontract administrator compares the returned document with the issued version for altered terms or reservations of rights, files it in the document system and marks the commitment as executed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: ERP posts the revised commitment
steps.description: The ERP adds the executed change to the subcontract commitment and job cost committed amounts, so the trade can bill it on its next progress invoice and the change appears in the monthly cost forecast.

evidence.note: Standard construction ERP behaviour.

steps.name: Tell site and accounting the change is executed
steps.description: The assistant project manager notifies the superintendent and the project accountant that the subcontract change is executed and can be billed, and closes the change record in the platform.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Reject the request in writing
steps.description: The project manager writes to the trade explaining why the work is in scope, unsubstantiated or not agreed, citing the subcontract clauses and site records. The letter keeps the record straight if the trade later liens or claims.

error.defect_description: Reason not tied to a contract clause.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the trade's reply
steps.description: The trade accepts the rejection, comes back with new evidence or escalates to a formal claim. Unresolved extras often resurface at closeout or as a lien.

evidence.note: 48% of specialty contractors have had change disputes escalate to arbitration or legal process; shares here are per change and are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Operations manager reviews the escalated extra
steps.description: The operations manager reviews the trade's escalated claim with the project manager and decides whether to settle, hold it for the closeout account or refer it to the claims manager.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority for disputes

next.condition: referred to claims or held to closeout

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Instruct the trade to proceed on time and materials
steps.description: For urgent work the superintendent issues a written site instruction telling the trade to proceed and record labour, equipment and materials daily, with a not-to-exceed value set by the project manager.

evidence.note: Directed work before price agreement mirrors the owner change directive; 97% of specialty contractors sometimes start before approval (Clearstory).

steps.name: Sign daily time and materials tickets
steps.description: The superintendent checks each day's ticket against the crew and equipment actually on the work and signs it. The trade then prices the signed tickets into a change order request.

error.defect_description: Tickets signed for hours not worked or for base-contract work.

evidence.note: The trade then takes on average 22 days from a signed T&M tag to a priced request.

steps.name: Cancel the pricing and tell the trade
steps.description: When the owner does not proceed, the assistant project manager cancels the subcontract change record and tells the trade in writing that the priced work will not go ahead. Any pricing costs are handled under the subcontract terms.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Quote revision loop
exceptions.description: The trade's quote goes back for revision because of missing backup or excess markup, adding another wait.

exceptions.name: Urgent work on time and materials
exceptions.description: The trade proceeds on a site instruction and the change is priced from signed daily tickets afterwards.

exceptions.name: Owner withdraws the change
exceptions.description: The owner does not proceed and the priced trade change is cancelled.

exceptions.name: Disputed extra
exceptions.description: The trade rejects the contractor's refusal and escalates; unresolved extras feed liens and claims.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trade change logged to signed subcontract change order or closure
benchmarks.population: Subcontract changes on Canadian non-residential building projects, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate built from the Clearstory survey averages (22 days to price, 26 days from request to signed change order), adjusted for changes that must wait for the owner change order.

benchmarks.population: US specialty contractors (survey with Dodge Construction Network), 2026

evidence.note: Published after the reference period; US.

benchmarks.population: US specialty contractors (survey with Dodge Construction Network), 2026

evidence.note: Published after the reference period; US.

pain_points.description: Trades wait for the owner change order before their own change is signed, so they work and finance extras for weeks.

evidence.note: 26 days average from request to signed change order; 43% wait three weeks or more; 83% say the process hurts cash flow.

pain_points.description: Quotes come back for repeated revisions over backup and markup.

evidence.note: More than half of requests need two or more revision cycles.

pain_points.description: Time and materials tickets signed late or for the wrong work start disputes.

evidence.note: Author's observation of common practice.

sources.title: 2026 State of Change Orders: Specialty Contractor Report
sources.supports: Survey of US general and specialty contractors: average 22 days from a signed T&M tag to a fully priced change order request; average 26 days from change order request submission to a signed change order from the GC; 43% wait three weeks or more; 97% sometimes start work before approval, 42% more than half the time; more than half of requests need two or more revision cycles; GCs cite disputed pricing (66%) and insufficient backup (53%) when reducing payment; 48% have had disputes escalate to arbitration or legal process.

sources.title: Construction Contract Modifications: A Joint Study by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Associated General Contractors of America
sources.publisher: Associated General Contractors of America and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
sources.supports: Contractor change registers overlaid on USACE change logs (vertical building and public works, design-bid-build and design-build): a general contractor submitted a proposal about 30 days after a request for proposal on average; the government issued the modification on average within 90 days of proposal receipt, median 55 days; causes include disagreement on merit, requests for more documentation, missing subcontractor pricing delaying proposals for weeks or months, and change volume exceeding staff; contractors log a change when notified by RFI response or submittal comment, on average 30 days before the government records it.

sources.title: Change Process for Construction Management Contracts (flowchart CA_MC_605_TRC)
sources.supports: Public owner change process: project team identifies a potential change through site instructions, RFIs or other methods; consultant prepares a change request with cost estimate and reasons, signed under expenditure signing authority; consultant issues a contemplated change notice for pricing; the construction manager prices it, obtaining subcontractor pricing; consultant and cost consultant review the quote in detail; if not agreed the change is not approved due to cost; otherwise a change authorization or change order is issued and the contractor proceeds.

sources.title: Change Directive (CD) Process (flowchart CA_MC_660_TRC)
sources.supports: For urgent changes the consultant prepares a change directive with a maximum upset price, signed under expenditure signing authority, directing the contractor to proceed before price is agreed; a final quotation is then requested and a change order issued; contractors cannot invoice against a change directive, only against an approved change order.

assumptions: Unit of work is one subcontract change, including pricing requests later cancelled because the owner did not proceed.
Owner-side pricing and negotiation are documented in gc-ops-change-order; s10 stands in for that wait here.
The Clearstory and Dodge survey is US and from 2026; it is used as the closest published measurement of trade change timing and shows the same mechanics as Canadian practice.
Subcontract administrators in supply chain key commitments; at some regional offices the assistant project manager does this directly.
Loops for revision and chasing restart the full wait for the trade's quote, which slightly overstates long tails.
Waits include nights and weekends; office roles work weekdays and superintendents work extended hours in season.

Simulated hands-on time (about 4.3 hours per change including revision loops) implies about 49 FTE against 43.3 stated; the gap is within the estimate's uncertainty and part of the review time overlaps owner-change pricing in gc-ops-change-order.
